correctness.rationale: The nine basis paths and their multiplication yield the displayed commutator matrix. All possible diagonal coincidences are partitioned; distinct eigenvalues yield rank six, exactly two equal give ranks four/five via unipotent conjugacy and cross-corner decompositions, and all equal give ranks zero through four via incidence and rank-two K matrices. The resulting polynomial sums to \(q^9\) symbolically. Exact independent path-basis matrix tests exhaust every radical six-tuple for representative diagonal patterns over orders 2,3,4,5. Full proof is field-independent; finite checks do not prove the family.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic database searches, accessible historical statement comparisons, and full-text examination of Chen–Van Oystaeyen–Zhang 2011, Shen 2014 and Dutta–Basnet–Nath 2015 uncovered no result implying the complete path-algebra adjoint rank polynomial. The closest same-object treatment computes a Green ring of modules, not centralizer spectra; the general commuting-probability work gives bounds, not this exact evaluation. The Taft 1971 original abstract was located but full text was not retrieved; this is recorded as a residual risk, not presented as complete noncoverage. Search nonmatches are not a uniqueness certificate.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete natural centralizer-size spectrum and commuting probability of the first nine-dimensional Loewy-three cyclic Nakayama algebra and its split Taft realization, not a sample numerical check. The full rank-five collision stratum comes from a nontrivial resonant two-path corner, absent in the radical-square-zero quotient, while radical support controls lower ranks. These exact distinctions facilitate commuting-pair and stratification studies and are not direct textbook dimension counting.
